prerequisites: Competencies from Algorithms and Data Structures module

learning_outcomes.text: Explain and apply scientific approaches to time series analysis to discover new and previously unknown temporal patterns.
Describe and compare the most important analysis methods such as Fourier and Wavelet analysis.
Explain statistical modeling possibilities for time series.
Apply methods to generate symbolic pattern descriptions from time series.
Apply scientific working methods (recognizing, formulating, solving problems, training abstraction skills).
Be able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Practical use of exploratory statistical methods for describing and analyzing data
Theory and practice of Fourier transformations for time series
Theory and practice of Wavelet transformations for time series
Neural Networks for time series analysis and forecasting

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercise assignments (at least 50% of points)
Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50% of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution for at least two exercise assignments. The final grade is based on an oral examination and is given on a scale of 0 to 15 points, according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Data Science degree program.

D.B. Percival, A.T Walden: Wavelet Methods for Time Series Analysis, Cambridge 2002.
J. Franke, W. Härdle, C. Hafner: Statistik der Finanzzeitreihen, Springer 2003.
J. Hartung, B. Elpelt: Multivariate Statistik, Oldenburg, 1999.
